item.title: Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
item.description:
Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
A Russian drone has struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern UkraineByVASILISA STEPANENKO Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 5:20 AM
Share
ZAPORIZHZHIA, Ukraine -- A Russian drone struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern Ukraine on Sunday, hitting a former school and nearby shelter that had been earlier blasted by multiple Russian guided bombs as residents waited for humanitarian aid, authorities said.
Ukraine said Monday's attack killed at least 55 people in the village of Komyshuvakha, near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region.
No one was injured in Sunday's strike on the same location, but specialized rescue equipment was damaged, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service.
Around 50 people were still listed as missing, Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, HUR, said. Many of the bodies recovered have not been identified and DNA analysis is ongoing.
Village resident Mykola Krasnov, 72, told The Associated Press on Saturday that he was still looking for his wife, but had heard no word from rescuers.
“She went to get humanitarian aid, and a 3-ton bomb was dropped there. Where is she?” he said. “She didn’t come home, and they didn’t find her body there. She isn’t in the morgue, and she isn’t here alive.”
HUR said Saturday that it had identified some of the Russian service members involved in the “double tap" strike with aerial bombs, which destroyed the former school and underground facility used by residents as shelter.
Ukraine has routinely accused Russia of conducting multiple strikes at the same site in quick succession to target emergency crews responding to the initial attack.
On Saturday, police officers and relatives gathered in Zaporizhzhia for a farewell ceremony for six officers killed in the Russian strikes on Komuyshuvakha, including three who died near the former school.

item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
item.description:
Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
Saudi Arabia has intercepted missiles targeting its capital, with debris damaging an Aramco building in RiyadhByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 5:05 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
Saudi Arabia intercepted incoming missiles targeting the kingdom's capital and other regions on Sunday, with falling debris damaging a building belonging to the state-owned oil giant Aramco in Riyadh’s financial district.
No casualties were reported. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels, who have claimed such attacks in the past.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates said it rescued 22 crew members after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship in the Sea of Oman, as risks to commercial shipping in the region remain high amid the war in the Middle East.
In Israel, President Isaac Herzog tapped Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival and the country's former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form the next government, dealing another blow to the incumbent prime minister in the wake of the Oct. 27 election.
Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Sunday. Read our full coverage here.
Witnesses in Riyadh said they heard a loud explosion on Sunday morning and described damage across multiple floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh. Some floors appeared to be heavily damaged and others showed damage to the exterior glass.
The witnesses spoke on condition of anonymity because of security concerns.
The Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles targeting Riyadh and other regions early Sunday, accusing the Houthis of launching the ballistic missiles.
The Saudi energy ministry said the attempted attack resulted in “falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building.” It added that there were no casualties....

item.title: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Argentina
item.description:
Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Argentina
Pope Leo XIV is wrapping up his visit to Uruguay by marking an important Catholic feast day that is tied to the country’s independenceByNICOLE WINFIELD Associated Press and NAYARA BATSCHKE Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 4:57 AM
MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay -- MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay (AP) — Pope Leo XIV is wrapping up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by marking an important Catholic feast day that is tied to the country’s independence, capping his effort to draw attention to the role the church has played in Latin America’s most secular country.
Leo was traveling to the city of Florida, north of Montevideo, before heading to Argentina for the second leg of his three-nation tour of South America. It's expected to be the most politically delicate, given the Catholic Church's sharp criticisms of the austerity program of libertarian President Javier Milei.
For his final event in Uruguay, Leo was commemorating the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three. Every year, thousands of pilgrims flock to the city to pray before the small wooden icon of the Virgin Mary.
According to tradition, 33 independence patriots acquired the Guaraní statue and had it with them when independence was declared from the Brazilian empire in Florida on Aug. 25, 1825.
Leo became the first pope in nearly four decades to visit Uruguay, in hopes of reminding its people that the Catholic Church is part of their very identity as a nation — even if in subsequent decades the country went on a deeply secular, and at times anticlerical, route.
Leo was hoping to leave a final parting message before opening the second leg of his South American trip, which he went ahead with despite having undergone surgery Oct. 13 to remove a cancerous tumor from his lung. The final stop is in Peru, his second homeland.

item.title: Bus overturns on a highway in Croatia, killing at least 2 people and injuring scores
item.description:
Bus overturns on a highway in Croatia, killing at least 2 people and injuring scores
Croatian police say that at least two people were killed and several were injured when a bus overturned on a highwayByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 3:39 AM
Share
ZAGREB, Croatia -- At least two people were killed and several were injured when a bus overturned on a highway in Croatia on Sunday, police said.
The bus with Serbian license plates skidded off the road and overturned at 7:25 a.m. while traveling in the direction of the Croatian capital, Zagreb, police said. The reason for the accident was not immediately clear.
The A3 highway in Croatia leads from the Serbian border, by Zagreb and toward Slovenia.

item.title: Poles mourn rare mass killing as authorities say attacker had far-right views
item.description:
Poles mourn rare mass killing as authorities say attacker had far-right views
Poland is in mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15ByBEATA ZAWRZEL Associated Press, RAFAL NIEDZIELSKI Associated Press, and CLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 3:35 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KRAKOW, Poland -- Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15 others before police shot and wounded him.
The attack, which Poland’s defense minister described as an “act of terror,” happened on Saturday in Main Square, which is in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town and is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city.
By evening, mourners had left candles in memory of the victims. The square remained partially closed on Sunday morning as authorities continued their investigation.
Authorities also found three dead bodies at the man's family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. The police said on Sunday they were the bodies of the attacker's sister, mother and father.
The family members likely died from gunshot wounds, the police said.
Four women and two men were killed in the Main Square shooting. Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, Krzysztof Jan Klęczar, the Malopolska regional governor, said on Sunday. A man from the U.K. and a woman from an unidentified foreign country were also among the dead.
The two police officers who stopped the attacker, in actions authorities hailed as heroic, remain in hospital. One of them is still in a coma while the other woke up from a coma, Klęczar said. Officials launched an appeal for blood donations for the benefit of the most seriously wounded policeman.

item.title: Taiwan detains a Communist Party leader over alleged Chinese sponsorship in election
item.description:
Taiwan detains a Communist Party leader over alleged Chinese sponsorship in election
Authorities in Taiwan have detained the leader of the Taiwan People’s Communist PartyByTAIJING WU Associated Press and KANIS LEUNG Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 3:24 AM
Share
TAIPEI, Taiwan -- Authorities in Taiwan detained the leader of the island's Taiwan People’s Communist Party, accusing him of running as a candidate for borough chief under the direction and sponsorship of China’s Communist Party, local media reported Sunday.
Taiwan is set to hold elections for mayors and local area chiefs on November 28. While the races focus more on livelihood issues, the results could be a good indicator of the popularity of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party under the leadership of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te ahead of the presidential election in 2028.
According to Taiwan's Central News Agency, prosecutors said in a statement Sunday that an initial investigation showed Taiwan People’s Communist Party chair Lin Te-wang also had directed another party member to run as a candidate for chief in another borough.
Prosecutors also alleged that Lin sought to buy votes by repeatedly recruiting voters to travel to mainland China, where they received hospitality, the report said.
While Lin’s party is not influential on the democratic island, it was not his first legal trouble over his alleged links with China. He and another party leader had faced charges of Chinese infiltration and attempting to influence elections but were found not guilty in 2025, the Taipei Times reported.
Taiwan’s Central News Agency said the prosecutors had received intelligence about foreign interference in the election and summoned 14 people and nine witnesses. item.title: New Zealanders won't know for weeks who won the election as neither side secures clear victory
item.description:
New Zealanders won't know for weeks who won the election as neither side secures clear victory
New Zealanders face weeks of uncertainty after Saturday's election, with no clear winner emergingByCHARLOTTE GRAHAM-MCLAY Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 12:51 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
WELLINGTON, New Zealand -- New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday’s election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.
The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's center-right National party and center-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before. On Saturday's numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.
The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years. Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.
Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power. It was a staggering ascension for a party that made three failed attempts at Parliament before Wong became leader less than a year ago.

item.title: Drone attack on a Colombian military base leaves 3 soldiers dead
item.description:
Drone attack on a Colombian military base leaves 3 soldiers dead
A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia killed three soldiers and injured at least 8, Colombia’s army saidByThe Associated PressNovember 7, 2026, 4:21 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BOGOTA, Colombia -- A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia killed three soldiers and injured at least eight, Colombia’s army said in a statement Saturday.
Authorities have not said who carried out the attack in Santa Rosa del Sur, a small town on the foothills of the San Lucas mountain range. The area around Santa Rosa is rich in gold mines and has long been disputed by the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army and smaller groups led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.
Footage shared on social media showed clouds of smoke emerging from the base following three explosions, and soldiers seeking protection in shelters made from sandbags.
“Those who were behind this attack … will have nowhere to hide,” President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a post on X Saturday. “Every attack against our soldiers strengthens our resolve to defend Colombia.”
Violence has intensified in several rural areas of Colombia since de la Espriella took office in August.
The conservative leader cancelled peace talks with the nation’s remaining rebel groups and has taken a more confrontational approach that includes using more airstrikes, militarizing some cities and creating joint task forces to defend strategic assets, including a pipeline that runs from the Caribbean coast to central Colombia.

item.title: Paraguay's former president faces prosecutors after his removal over bank collapse
item.description:
Paraguay's former president faces prosecutors after his removal over bank collapse
Paraguay's former President Santiago Peña has been taken to the attorney general’s office for questioningByThe Associated PressNovember 7, 2026, 10:45 AM
Paraguay’s former president was taken to the attorney general’s office for questioning Saturday, just hours after being ousted by Congress over the collapse of a major bank. The Central Bank said it was working to compensate hundreds of thousands of people who were locked out of their accounts this week.
Drone footage taken by Paraguay’s Telefuturo showed ousted President Santiago Peña arriving at the attorney general’s compound in a black SUV, escorted by police officers. He wore navy blue pants and a white shirt and was not handcuffed.
Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday ordered the arrest of Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was transferred to a military base late Friday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside his home.
The arrest order was issued soon after the Senate removed Peña from office in a unanimous vote. The verdict came just three days after regulators seized Ueno Bank, freezing nearly 3 million customers’ access to their savings and triggering a political crisis.
Peña was replaced by Vice President Pedro Alliana, who began naming a new Cabinet Saturday. The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received partial or full reimbursement of their insured deposits under Paraguayan law.
Lawmakers accused Peña of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending. Peña has denied wrongdoing.
